physicalNotes: Radius: Rp/R* 0.15883 (Challener et al. 2024, ApJL 969, L32, Table 1, fitted to the white-light transit) times the host record's 462,640.5 km. A sphere: tidal and rotational flattening are not modelled. GM from the assumed planet mass 2.052 Jupiter masses (same table) times Jupiter's GM 126,686,534 km^3/s^2 (JPL).

sources.period: Challener et al. (2024), Table 1, assumed orbital period 0.8134741 d, matching Hammond et al. (2024)
sources.shape: Challener et al. (2024), Table 1: semi-major axis 4.8767 +0.0068/-0.0069 stellar radii and inclination 82.155 +/- 0.027 degrees fitted to the white-light transit; eccentricity 0 assumed
sources.phase: Challener et al. (2024), Table 1: transit time 55934.2922503 BMJD_TDB
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north). The orbit passes the stellar disc on the side Challener et al. (2024) assume for their map (footnote 1): their map's north is the orbit normal's side as constructed here.
